basis: The two diffs are byte-identical in every executable line — same hunk header (@@ -939,26 +939,28 @@), same single semantic fix (`and 0xFE` -> `and 0xFD` in the `cp 0x00`/a1 branch of clrCastleSq, so a1 traffic clears bit1=WQ instead of bit0=WK), same untouched masks on the h1/a8/h8 branches, same two added comment lines plus four added branch comments. A mechanical diff of the two blocks shows differences ONLY in comment prose. Both are equally minimal (one byte of semantics), equally correct for the reported defect (fixes the phantom rook, restores WQ revocation, stops the spurious WK revocation), and equally clear. The only discriminator is comment style, and it does not separate the processes: X writes an interface-contract header naming the register parameters ("clrCastleSq(A=square, B=rights) - a move from or to a corner square kills the right that corner owns"), which reads spec-like; Y states the same rule behaviourally ("a rook leaving or being captured on a corner kills THAT corner's right") and adds a traceability pointer ("see chess.asm"), which also reads like a stated invariant with a source-of-truth reference. Either author could plausibly have written either header. There is no process residue in the source changes — no assertions, no conformance-suite or spec artefacts, no extra guards, no restated theorem, no difference in scope or defensive coverage. Attributing authorship here would mean inferring process from punctuation and phrasing, so I decline to guess.
